title: Patient Care Desk Guidance: Waiting Allowance on Prescriptions Strength-Error Remakes
content:
A patient whose Kestrel Prescriptions fill was confirmed as the wrong strength may wait some days between the pharmacist's review and the remake. The strength-error waiting allowance covers that wait.

## The rule applied at the desk

The strength-error waiting allowance counts the calendar days from the review date of the answered report, as day 0, to today:

- **3 or more days** give that same number of days;
- **one day up to fewer than 3 days** gives 1 day;
- **a remake on the review date** gives no days.

Each allowance day adds the prescribed daily units — the prescription's written quantity divided by its written days supply — to the strength-error remake quantity.

## Ladder (hypothetical review on day 0, 2 prescribed daily units)

| Today | Days from review | Allowance days | Units added |
|---|---|---|---|
| day 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| day 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| day 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 |
| day 3 | 3 | 3 | 6 |
| day 8 | 8 | 8 | 16 |

## Points of judgement

**Which review date?** The review date of the report the remake answers.

**The remake is made two days after the review.** Two days is one day up to fewer than 3, so the allowance is 1 day, not 2.

**The remake is made three days after the review.** Three days reaches 3, so the allowance is the full 3 days.
